scope: Phase four: time, key, Script, Animation, Message, Attribute and Synchro/State/Critical Section values
status: Implemented and validated on macOS arm64 Release. Both eleven-group paired timing and the same-program control pass the original 3% limits. Phase four remains in progress.
implemented: Time retains native float milliseconds, including fractional milliseconds and negative values. Editing one unit does not truncate untouched units. Key values retain DirectInput scan codes, with UI-backend-independent ImGui capture and native display names.

Script owners/classes, animation objects, message types, attribute categories and synchronization objects are copied by read-only queries. Nested records use the same editors. The default filters follow the current value; explicit null owner and empty category retain their distinct meaning.

New message names and synchronization objects stay in the existing value draft. Acceptance registers message types, creates ordinary objects and applies explicit rendezvous-count changes through existing core commands inside one Edit. The native row creation/user flags and direct setters are removed.

Registered message names and displayed rendezvous counts belong to the referenced resource. Parameter-only history does not restore those unedited fields. Explicit signed native count edits, object creation and parameter changes share one undo step. An unchanged explicit count preserves Dirty and Redo; successful NoChange also refreshes the native working value.

Editor C interface version 13 adds an explicit nullable object-argument field. A required argument may contain null without allowing omission. Registration rejects invalid annotations or provider disagreements. Scalar choice schemas remain checked; record editors declare their own copied choice projection. Public headers still contain no STL, SDK, SDL or ImGui dependency.

Curve/dependency controls and the remaining editors share the existing full-target presentation reset helper. Script owner references and key capture use fixed window keys. Escape, clicking outside or the Cancel button, stopping capture, focus loss and inline reappearance actively cancel capture; later key events do not write an old draft.

An independent C module replaces all seven query/editor/modifier sets and the selection query. Native dialogs retain the captured providers after configuration changes. Opaque native parameter copying and file formats remain unchanged.
Runtime SDK sources, pre-existing SDK changes/untracked contents and all GPU rendering/transfer production files are unchanged.

checks.core_cases: Forty time updates before one acceptance, native byte-exact undo, fractions, negative milliseconds, invalid values, derived types, key bounds, required nullable reference clearing and omitted-argument rejection, script owner defaults and filtering, animation class checks, message registration deferred until acceptance and stable native indices, read-only message names and synchronization counts across history, all three synchronization object classes, signed count changes, unchanged-count Redo retention, nested values and member identity, and cancelled creations.
checks.public_headers: C and C++ consume nullable object parameters with matching layout; invalid nullable descriptors and inconsistent providers are rejected.

initial_failures.reason: A new regression reproduced the key capture blocking the Cancel button. Clicking outside, stopping capture and reappearing now actively cancel the draft, and the final complete suite passes.
The restricted run aborted without a diagnostic. The desktop-enabled rerun reported the record choice-schema mismatch; no production startup workaround was added.
Record editors were incorrectly limited to scalar choice-list schemas. Record-specific projections now retain required target/scope checks without the scalar pairing assumption.
Clearing script/animation references was rejected as a missing required object. Explicit nullability now accepts null and still rejects an omitted argument.
Confirmed the same missing nullable argument declaration before its correction.
The optional filter record was refused when an independent caller omitted it. Both omission and an empty record now select the documented defaults.

checks.native_cleanup: Previously reported native file-menu cleanup crashes did not reproduce in these complete runs; no root-cause fix is claimed.

performance.scope: Unchanged cubes64 Release editor-frame benchmark; eleven paired groups, at least fifteen seconds of warmup per process and one second per group. No builds or CTest suites ran during capture.
performance.reference_preparation: Before editing, git archive froze 4c5bfc9 and the existing built runtime/lib directories were copied. The copied CMakeCache metadata identifies the frozen source. Both source and binary hashes identify the measured programs.
performance.sdk_change_option: --sdk-change permits the pre-existing dirty runtime SDK. This batch does not change it; all sixteen recursive states and both sets of twenty-two runtime hashes match.

prior_source_measurements.scope: Both passed before the final mouse-cancel regression and capture fix; retained as earlier source versions, not final acceptance.

performance.unmeasured: Application allocations, GPU-only preserve/pass/submit counts and retain/native-query counts are not measured by this harness. No additional zero-allocation or all-counter claim is made.

remaining: DataArray table and remaining Setup/Schematic/Layout migration stays in phase four. completed_phase remains three.
The pre-existing native cleanup fault remains unresolved.
Cross-platform execution and additional GPU/allocation counters retain their existing coverage gaps.
